questions.topic: eGurukul · Structure of Skeletal Muscle Cell
questions.stem: A neurologist strikes the tendons of various muscles to check the stretch reflex in a patient of stroke, the receptor involved is primarily regulating:
questions.solutionHtml:
Length
  • When a skeletal muscle with an intact nerve supply is stretched, it contracts. This response is called the stretch reflex or myotatic reflex.
  • The stimulus that initiates this reflex is the stretch of the muscle, and the response is  the contraction of the muscle being stretched. The sense organ is a small encapsulated spindle-like or a fusiform-shaped structure called the muscle spindle, located within the fleshy part of the muscle.
  • The impulses originating from the spindle are transmitted to the CNS by fast sensory fibers that pass directly to the motor neurons that supply the same muscle. The neurotransmitter at the central synapse is glutamate.
  • This sense organ is involved in signaling changes in the length of the muscle in which it is located. Changes in muscle length are associated with changes in joint angle; thus, muscle spindles provide information on position (i.e., proprioception).


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition, Page Number: 688.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Structure of Skeletal Muscle Cell
questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy presents with abnormal running, jumping, and hopping. His parents have observed that he uses his arms to climb up his legs when rising from the floor. The pediatrician suspects Duchenne muscular dystrophy, and electromyography confirms a myopathy. The amount of force produced by a skeletal muscle can be increased by which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Decreasing the interval between contractions

When the interval between skeletal muscle contractions is small, the force produced by the two successive contractions will summate.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 77.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Structure of Skeletal Muscle Cell
questions.stem: A 12-year-old male with muscular dystrophy is found to have a mutation of the gene that encodes the protein dystrophin. Genetic alterations in dystrophin lead to progressive muscular weakness because dystrophin provides structural support to the sarcolemma by binding which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Actin to β-dystroglycan
  • The large dystrophin protein forms a rod that connects the thin actin filaments to the transmembrane protein β-dystroglycan in the sarcolemma by smaller proteins in the cytoplasm, syntrophins.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 65–68, 77

questions.topic: eGurukul · Structure of Skeletal Muscle Cell
questions.stem: In the department of Physiology of a medical college, an experiment was conducted. In which a muscle was extracted and suspended in a physiological solution. The muscle taken does not contract spontaneously. But when directly stimulated by an electrode the muscle contracts. The muscle also continues to contract upon stimulation after being treated by a drug that antagonizes myosin light chain kinase activity. Based on the data provided, what type of muscle tissue was being tested in the experiment?
questions.solutionHtml:
Skeletal muscle

Skeletal muscles contract after stimulation. So the correct answer is B as other options are ruled out.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology Edition 14th; Page number 82

questions.topic: eGurukul · Structure of Skeletal Muscle Cell
questions.stem: Suppose you are experimenting with skeletal muscle preparation. You want to measure isotonic contractions in that skeletal muscle preparation. Increasing the length of the preparation beyond the optimal length before the electrical stimulation would produce which of the following changes to active and passive tension?

options.label: A
options.text: Increase active tension and increase passive tension

options.label: B
options.text: Increase active tension and decrease passive tension

options.label: C
options.text: Decrease active tension and increase passive tension

options.label: D
options.text: Decrease active tension and decrease passive tension

questions.answerText: Decrease active tension and increase passive tension
questions.solutionHtml:
Decrease active tension and increase passive tension
  • As the sarcomere is stretched, elastic elements of the sarcomere are passively stretched, and tension increases. So the passive tension increases
  • Active tension decreases because as the sarcomere is stretched, the actin and myosin overlap decreases and on stimulation fewer cross-bridges form, and thus less active tension is produced.
  • So the correct option with the correct combination is C.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology Edition 14th; Page number 80.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Structure of Skeletal Muscle Cell
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a Sarcolemmal protein?
questions.solutionHtml:
Perlecan
  • Perlecan is not a Sarcolemmal protein.
  • Perlecan, a large basement membrane heparan sulfate proteoglycan, is expressed in a wide array of tissues where it regulates diverse cellular processes including bone formation, inflammation, cardiac development, and angiogenesis.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 96.
